newsitem.title: UK: Belfast "peace boy" weeps over N.Ireland bomb.
newsitem.headline: Belfast "peace boy" weeps over N.Ireland bomb.

text.p: The Belfast boy whose plea for peace captured the heart of President Bill Clinton said his dream had died with the double car bomb that injured 31 people at Northern Ireland army headquarters.
"The terrorists haven't given peace a chance," weeping 12-year-old David Sterrett told the Daily Mirror after Monday's blasts cast a giant shadow over the already fragile peace process.
Protestant Sterrett and eight-year-old Catholic Catherine Hammill joined hands to plead for peace when Clinton visited Belfast last November as hopes for peace were high.
But the child said his illusions were now shattered.

"I am horrified. I feel sick inside. I cannot believe the IRA are so stupid as to go back to bombing and killing again. They have let the kids of Ulster down. President Clinton will be horrified and feel let down by them too," he said.

"I think my dream has died now. All my friends are frightened," he told the paper after the suspected Irish Republican guerrilla attack. "My big fear is everyone will now start killing. I just hope they all see sense."
